body: state.inspect under the Rust engine dispatches a fixed set of events (as of 2026-05-22): mem_read (after, IRExpr::Load), mem_write (after, IRStmt::Store), reg_read (after, IRExpr::Get), reg_write (after, IRStmt::Put), instruction (before, IRStmt::IMark), irsb (before, execute_block_with_callbacks entry), exit (before, IRStmt::Exit). The dispatcher (RustExplorationManager._dispatch_inspect_event) takes **attrs kwargs. Per-event _cb_inspect_<event> handlers build their own SimInspector attrs dict. Bitmask layout in _INSPECT_EVENT_BITS: mem_read=0, mem_write=1, reg_read=2, reg_write=3, exit=5, instruction=6, irsb=7 (bit 4 reserved for future fork). Bits 0..=5 mirror crate::state::InspectEvent; bits 6,7 are custom (no InspectionManager enum slot). Other events (call, fork, return, syscall, constraints, simprocedure, dirty, address_concretization, expr, statement, tmp_read, tmp_write, vex_lift, symbolic_variable, engine_process, memory_page_map) still raise NotImplementedError at registration.
reason: Stable user-facing supported-event matrix; fits rust_engine.rst alongside other limitation tables.

body: RustExplorationManager treats certain SimOptions as hard failures and raises NotImplementedError at construction (via _check_raise_options) rather than warn-once. Current raise list: (1) TRACK_*_ACTIONS family — TRACK_MEMORY_ACTIONS, TRACK_REGISTER_ACTIONS, TRACK_TMP_ACTIONS, TRACK_JMP_ACTIONS, TRACK_OP_ACTIONS, TRACK_ACTION_HISTORY; (2) CONCRETIZE — BatchedConcretizationBacker semantics not available in Rust; (3) CONSERVATIVE_WRITE_STRATEGY — Rust SymbolicMemory always concretizes within strategy limits; (4) DO_RET_EMULATION — Rust does not emulate rets so the emulated successor is silently missing; (5) CALLLESS — Rust has no call-skip path so Callable steps into callee; (6) EFFICIENT_STATE_MERGING — Rust does not drive SimStateHistory's strongref path so ancestor-ref retention is silently dropped (Veritesting auto-adds this option). The check is hooked into both __init__ (initial states) and _add_rust_state (late additions). Default-mode bundle members (TRACK_CONSTRAINT_ACTIONS, TRACK_MEMORY_MAPPING, SIMPLIFY_MERGED_CONSTRAINTS) must never be added to the raise list — would break every entry_state(). SIMPLIFY_MERGED_CONSTRAINTS is honored implicitly through Python state.merge() fallback. TRACK_OP_ACTIONS ships in the fastpath mode bundle — fastpath users hit the raise and must drop to the Python engine.
reason: Stable unsupported-options matrix maintained for users; rust_engine.rst already has a SimOption coverage section.
